note: std-drive over two keyed std-http-client traits (std-http-keyed): the service-account token is a jwt-bearer grant and the user token a refresh_token grant (credential-connect) the host credential store mints and renews, carried by the DriveSaHttp and DriveUserHttp credentials, never by an event; every call is a row of DriveCall under its own key; a not-held token mints once and sends again, a second not-held answer falls back to the other credential (reads and shares service account first, uploads and folders user first) and, with both spent, asks credential-status about the refresh token; list, metadata and media reads retry under keyed std-retry (4 attempts, 100 x 5^(n-1) ms capped at 1500: 100, 500, 1500) and the media read starts when std-retry completes the metadata run; the upload body is one multipart/related body built in .lolo. Self-handled internal events (declared -> internal) are consumed by the trait and not listed.

cases.note: a list and a get are both in flight under std-retry; each key has its own run, so the second start schedules its own first retry instead of being ignored by a run busy with the first.
each call asks the store itself; one call hearing the answer never settles the other call.
the metadata reply is stored and std-retry's completion of the metadata run starts the media read under the same key; the media request goes out on the same credential.
the call counter gives each call its own key, so two identical lists are two rows with two retry runs and two replies.
